log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out, which blunts the opponent's physical attackers like Garchomp and Kingambit. Garchomp is the fastest and hardest-hitting physical threat, and Gholdengo gives strong special coverage, including Thunderbolt against the Steel/Dragon and Ground-weak targets on their side.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since the opponent team mirrors mine, I need to pick three strong picks from my six. Garchomp with its mega stone offers speed and power, Kingambit hits hard, Incineroar brings Intimidate and Fake Out support, and Gholdengo is a strong special attacker—I'm weighing which trio forms the best core against their matching squad.

I'll keep it straightforward: Incineroar as the lead for Intimidate and Fake Out pressure, paired with Garchomp and Gholdengo for solid offensive coverage against their mirrored team.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is slower than the opposing Garchomp, which may be faster than it. Fake Out has +3 priority, so it hits first, flinches Garchomp, and gives Incineroar a free turn. Flare Blitz is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon typing.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Fake Out works turn 1 since it's a fresh switch-in, flinching Garchomp while chipping some damage despite the opponent's attack drop. It's a safe standard lead move here, so I'll go with Fake Out.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is faster than Incineroar and Flare Blitz is resisted, so attacking with Incineroar is poor. Parting Shot lowers the opposing Garchomp's Attack and Special Attack by one stage and pivots out. That brings in our Garchomp, which is faster and resists the opponent's Ground attacks, letting it take a hit and punish with a Mega.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Mega Garchomp is at 87% HP with its attack lowered from Intimidate, and being Dragon/Ground it resists Incineroar's Flare Blitz. It also outspeeds our Garchomp, and I'm noting the ability difference between the two Garchomps—sand force on theirs versus rough skin on ours.

Earthquake from Mega Garchomp would hit Incineroar hard too, and I'm weighing options: Protect to scout, or Parting Shot to drop its stats further while switching into Gholdengo. If I bring Gholdengo in after Parting Shot, Earthquake becomes a 2x weakness against its Steel typing, but the stacked Attack drops (-1 from Intimidate, -1 more from Parting Shot) might let Gholdengo survive the hit given its bulk.

Protect would just deny damage this turn but costs a scouting turn, while Flare Blitz isn't threatening since it's resisted and carries recoil. I'm also considering bringing my own Garchomp in after Parting Shot, since Ground-type attacks won't touch it due to its typing.

Weighing it against just switching straight into Gholdengo, Parting Shot still looks like the cleaner play—it salvages value from Incineroar before it goes down and sets up my Garchomp to threaten back. I'll go with Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Incineroar can't act usefully, so I must switch. Gholdengo takes 2x from the opposing Garchomp's Earthquake, while my Garchomp resists nothing relevant but takes neutral damage, has 169 Speed to likely outrun it, and can hit back with Outrage for 2x.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar sits at 100/202 after Sitrus healing, while Mega Garchomp is at 87% with its Attack and Special Attack dropped. Earthquake clearly hit hard before the berry activated, so I need to weigh switching to my own Garchomp against staying in.

Gholdengo could tank a weakened Earthquake since Garchomp's Attack is down at -2, though Ground still deals 2x to Steel, so it'd take a meaningful chunk off its 164 HP. My own Garchomp outspeeds the Mega at base 102 with my 169, which matters against its Sand Force boosted attacks.

Incineroar has no good way to stay in at this HP and must switch out, leaving the choice between Gholdengo (weak to Earthquake) or my Garchomp (neutral to Earthquake and faster), making the latter the safer switch.

Given the opposing Garchomp's attack is lowered, switching in my Garchomp looks like the right call.

decisions.thought: We move first at 169 Speed, and their Mega Garchomp (at 87%, with -2 Attack) is likely in KO range. Outrage is super effective because Dragon hits their Dragon/Ground typing for 2x, so it should knock it out. Mega Evolving would drop our Speed, so I'll skip it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
The opponent's Garchomp is already mega, already weakened to 87% with lowered attack and special attack stats. Since they've used their mega, I'm free to mega evolve our own Garchomp, and our speed advantage means we'd still act first either way.

Outrage is the key consideration here since Dragon-type is super effective against their Dragon/Ground typing, while Earthquake would only be neutral against them. With their Garchomp already damaged and stat-lowered, Outrage looks like the stronger offensive choice to finish the job.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action is available: Outrage. Garchomp is faster than Archaludon (169 vs 94-150), and Dragon-type Outrage is super effective against Archaludon's Dragon typing, so it should hit hard first.

Garchomp fainted, so I must switch. Gholdengo is at full HP and is faster than Archaludon's likely speed. Its Thunderbolt is super effective on the Steel half of Archaludon, and Archaludon's SpA is at -2, so it can take a hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I need to pick between Incineroar at half health or full-health Gholdengo with its strong special attack. Checking Archaludon's typing, Steel/Dragon is vulnerable to Fire, Fighting, and Ground, so Incineroar's Fire moves could hit hard despite its lower SpA stat being less relevant here.

Actually, Gholdengo's Thunderbolt is super effective against Steel, and with its SpA of 203 plus Life Orb, that's a huge hit—especially since Archaludon's SpA is already lowered. Gholdengo also resists most of what Archaludon throws back, including Draco Meteor, so switching to Gholdengo looks like the clear play.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is Steel/Dragon, so Make It Rain and Thunderbolt are resisted and Gholdengo's Steel attack would self-drop Sp. Atk. Shadow Ball is neutral with Life Orb and 203 Sp. Atk, and Gholdengo is likely faster, so it should deal heavy damage to the 57% Archaludon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Archaludon's Steel/Dragon typing against Thunderbolt and Shadow Ball — Electric is resisted by Steel so that's weakened, while Shadow Ball looks neutral since Steel doesn't resist Ghost.

Shadow Ball with Life Orb and 203 SpA probably deals somewhere around 40-55% to Archaludon's remaining HP, not a guaranteed knockout, while Make It Rain gets resisted by the Steel typing too. Since Draco Meteor's SpA drop hurts Archaludon and Gholdengo is weak to Dragon-type attacks, I'm settling on firing off Shadow Ball as the safest, strongest option here.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo outspeeds Incineroar (136 vs 72-123), so it moves first. Shadow Ball and Make It Rain are both poor into Fire/Dark, and Make It Rain also drops Sp. Atk. Thunderbolt is neutral against Fire/Dark and gives the strongest reliable damage without a self-debuff.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm noting the opponent's Incineroar has mega evolved at 69% HP, confirming it retains Intimidate and checking its stat spread against the observed speed range to verify it matches the Mega form.

Gholdengo's options: Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark, Make It Rain's Steel typing is resisted by Fire, but Thunderbolt hits neutrally and benefits from Life Orb boost, making it the best damage option. Since Good as Gold blocks status moves like Parting Shot, I lean toward Thunderbolt for reliable pressure rather than risking a setup move like Nasty Plot.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has fainted, so the only legal action is switching in Incineroar. I must submit that switch.

Only Incineroar is left on our side, so Parting Shot would just fail. The opposing Mega Incineroar is at about 63 HP, and Flare Blitz is our only real damage, so it may bring the target down this turn. Fake Out does too little, and Protect only delays.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Incineroar is at 100/202 HP, opponent's Mega Incineroar at 31%. I'm checking whether Fake Out is actually usable here since it requires being the first turn on the field, but our Incineroar has been out since turn 6, so I need to verify if it's genuinely legal despite appearing in the move list.

I'm estimating Flare Blitz damage against the opponent's Mega Incineroar, factoring in resisted Fire-type STAB and its -1 Atk from Intimidate, landing somewhere around 50 damage which might not secure the KO given their remaining HP, plus the 33% recoil cost to consider. I'm also weighing Parting Shot as an alternative, since it would drop their stats further and let me pivot out safely.

Blitz might not secure the KO given uncertain defense and speed ranges. Protect could be safer to scout, since the opponent's recoil from Flare Blitz will chip them down further anyway even if they hit me for moderate damage.

Fake Out is tempting for the flinch but only deals minor damage, so going with Flare Blitz for the kill potential makes more sense.

decisions.thought: Archaludon outspeeds us (94-150 vs 80), and our Incineroar at 39 HP is likely KO'd by its Dracometeor before Flare Blitz can move. Parting Shot has no bench to switch into, so it's useless as the last Pokémon. Protect blocks the incoming hit this turn and keeps Incineroar alive.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Incineroar is at 39/202 HP against a Mega Archaludon at 57%, which outspeeds us and could likely KO with Draco Meteor. I'm weighing whether Flare Blitz is worth it since Fire hits Steel super effectively, though it's neutral against the Dragon typing.

Since Archaludon moves first, Flare Blitz probably won't connect if we go down beforehand, so I'm checking our bench — but it looks like Incineroar is our last mon with Garchomp and Gholdengo already fainted, which means Parting Shot has no switch target and is essentially useless here. That leaves a choice between attacking with Flare Blitz or using Protect to stall one turn, though Protect doesn't recover HP and just delays the inevitable.

decisions.thought: Incineroar has 39 HP and Archaludon is faster and has Draco Meteor, which will likely knock it out. Flare Blitz is resisted by Steel and can't finish Archaludon at 57%, and Parting Shot has no bench to switch to. Protect blocks this turn's attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's my only option left at 39 HP, no viable switches since the bench is fainted. Opponent's mega Archaludon is faster and Steel-type, so Flare Blitz won't be very effective against it.

Parting Shot has no switch target to benefit from, and Draco Meteor would likely finish me off at this HP. Protect is the safest play here—it blocks this turn's attack, buying time even if it's only a temporary solution.
